title: Sequential coefficient localization is sheafified fraction localization
statement: Let C be a small site with topology J and sheaf of commutative rings R [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For U in C and f in R(U), the module-sheaf defined as the sequential colimit of O_U under multiplication by f [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization] is isomorphic to the sheafification of the fraction presheaf W↦R(W)[1/f|W] [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. The isomorphism is one of O_U-modules.

proof.text: Send x at stage n of the rank-one presheaf sequence to x/f^n in each sectionwise fraction localization. Localization restriction maps extend ring restrictions, so this is a natural compatible cocone.

source.place: Tag 0997, the sequential-colimit definition of A_f and its ordinary fraction interpretation.

proof.text: For any presheaf-module cocone, send x/f^n to the image of x from stage n. Equality of fractions means a further power of f annihilates the difference of cross products; transition compatibility makes the two cocone images equal. The maps are linear and commute with restriction, and uniqueness holds because every fraction has this form. Thus the fraction presheaf is the colimit. Zero and nilpotent denominators are included.

proof.text: Sheafification preserves colimits as a left adjoint. The isomorphic counit identifies the sheafified unit presheaf, and its multiplication map, with the actual unit sheaf and multiplication map. Consequently sheafifying the colimit in the previous step gives the recorded sequential localization.

theorem ringedSite_localization_fraction_comparison
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (U : C) (f : R.obj.obj (op U)) :
    let R₀ := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R
    Nonempty (ringedSiteSectionLocalization R₀ U f ≅
      ringedSectionLocalization (R.over U) (ringedSliceSection R U f))
